summary: Sets up front steering geometry for the left and right wheels. Searches the suspension component arrays for a matching pair by geometry identifier and component name, applies a 3D transform, then finds the closest geometry pair per side, applies the steering angle via a tan-based formula, and updates the rotation matrices for both wheels. Logs an error when the required eight components are not found.

operations.description: Outer loop over the two sides (v3 = 0, 1); selects per-side steering name: aFrSteering with count 12 for v3 != 0, aFlSteering with count 11 otherwise.
If this[1393] (suspension component element count at this+0x15C4) is <= 0, skip the component search and jump to the not-found error path.
Iterate the suspension component array at this[1394] (this+0x15C8) with a 72-byte (dword-index 18) stride.
Match a component pair whose ids equal the geometry identifier this[1404] (this+0x15F0) in either order, and whose name is empty or matches the steering name via sub_588410.
Call TransformApply3D to apply the component transform and record the matched pair into the local v62 array; accumulate the matched count v4 by two per match.
For each matched component compute its world position from the dot products of the component axes and store the three offsets into the pair record.
If the matched count v4 is not 8, and dword_7C569C != 5 and StringSplitLoop returns a printable frame, call DebugLogWrite with the aSorryOnlySuppo message.
For each side find the closest geometry pair from the matched records using a squared-distance search, copy the best pair, and store the midpoint between them.
Swap the two side records if the second side's ordering index is lower, so the primary pair is on the expected side.

Apply the steering angle via v31 = (tan(a2 per-side steering angle) * (primary - secondary distance) - (primary - secondary offset)) * 0.5; add v31 to the primary pair and subtract it from the secondary pair.
For both wheels, rebuild the 3x3 rotation matrix rows for each of the two records from the parent component axis dot products.
Increment the side counter and repeat until both sides are processed; return when the counter exceeds one.
